page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction support for AVX-512 vector extensions, bfloat16, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource provisioning includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is a bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch space and low-latency disk operations. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present in this profile, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Performance testing reflects strong single-core capabilities, registering a top-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 2080.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 3078.28. Multi-core performance aligns with expected mid-tier results for an 8-vCPU instance, achieving 8101.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 12313.93 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate high throughput for cached 16 KB reads at 607.39 GB/sec, though larger uncached 256 MB reads settle in the lower quartile at 38.85 GB/sec. Application testing shows 11.75 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 11.61 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The qualitative cost profile favors IO-intensive operations where onboard NVMe storage eliminates external block storage latency and data transfer overheads. The balanced allocation of 64 GB RAM and local NVMe capacity positions this instance effectively for transactional databases, NoSQL data stores, caching layers, and search index nodes requiring rapid local disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 64.0 GB of RAM alongside an integrated 1920 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile single-core CPU throughput, while multi-core compute and data-processing tasks fall within mid-tier expectations. Large uncached memory read bandwidth represents a relative bottleneck compared to cached operations. With its high memory-to-core allocation and fast local disk, the instance delivers solid resource density for transactional databases, distributed key-value caches, log indexing, and I/O-bound data pipelines.
